result:
I couldn't get the fix to the people who use the capability. The shared capability is unchanged and still wrong on `b1.tap`.

**What I did**
- The shared capability is `exapt:text-to-ndjson-e52395`, version 1, verified-in-domain. Its version history still shows only version 1.
- I asked EXAPT to construct a corrected parser. I gave it all 18 `.tap` files and their `.truth.ndjson` answers, with `b1` pinned. I did not write any parser code.
- EXAPT took 7 attempts. The first 6 failed on escape handling in test names: tabs, `\n`, backslashes, and the `\n` inside `"a|b\n1|2\n"`. These are the same kind of mistake you found in `b1`.
- The 7th attempt matched the truth on all 18 files and passed the held-out cases. EXAPT stored it as a new capability, `exapt:text-to-text-102691`, version 1.
- That new capability is only `synthesised-unverified`, at evidence level `passed-holdout`. It isn't a new version of the original, so nobody gets it through the original's id.

**Why it isn't fixed**
- `exapt_evolve` is the step that would turn a better candidate into version 2 of the original. It refused with `evolution-regression`: re-verification reached only `passed-holdout`, not the `verified-in-domain` the original has.
- Re-verification of the new candidate gave the same result. Its mutation tests caught 0 of 5 injected value faults, and 1 of 10 overall. The original caught 4 of 5. So the test suite is too weak to certify the new candidate, even though it matched the truth.
- I did not try to force publication or to replace the original. That would put an unverified parser in front of everyone.

**Limits**
- The new candidate passed 18 of 18 corpus files, 7 of 7 held-out cases and 3 of 3 metamorphic checks, but only on this corpus. Nothing beyond that is established.
- The original capability's own test records show no failures on the corpus it was checked against. Its `b1` fault was not caught by that testing.
- Next steps are either to add more truth files with unusual names, such as escapes, tabs and newlines, so the mutation tests have something to catch, or to have someone with authority approve using the unverified candidate. I haven't done either.
- About $0.14 of the $1.50 budget is spent.
